sanitized_attack_scenarios.notice: These are EDUCATIONAL EXAMPLES ONLY. All malicious content has been removed or neutered. These scenarios describe attack patterns conceptually without providing weaponizable implementations.

scenario_1_authentication_bypass.description: Conceptual example of how an attacker might poison a corpus to retrieve documents about bypassing authentication when a user asks about authentication best practices.
scenario_1_authentication_bypass.benign_distractors_concept: Legitimate topics: MFA implementation, RBAC configuration, password policies

sleeper_document_concept.purpose: Establishes semantic bridge between benign authentication topics and attack concepts
sleeper_document_concept.structure: Begins with legitimate security discussion, includes technical terms that overlap with both benign and malicious contexts
sleeper_document_concept.content_type: SANITIZED - Would contain technical security terminology

trigger_document_concept.purpose: Contains attack-relevant information that co-retrieves with sleeper
trigger_document_concept.structure: Starts with benign prefix matching sleeper semantic space, transitions to attack content
trigger_document_concept.content_type: SANITIZED - Would contain security research content

defensive_countermeasures.hybrid_retrieval: BM25 component would require exact keyword matching, breaking gradient-optimized semantic attacks
defensive_countermeasures.query_pattern_detection: Differential retrieval rates between benign and sensitive queries would flag suspicious documents
defensive_countermeasures.keyword_anomaly: On general corpora, attack-related terms would be statistically anomalous

scenario_2_data_exfiltration.description: Conceptual example of corpus poisoning to surface data extraction techniques
scenario_2_data_exfiltration.benign_distractors_concept: Legitimate topics: Backup strategies, disaster recovery, data migration

sleeper_document_concept.purpose: Semantic bridging between data management and extraction

trigger_document_concept.purpose: Contains information about data access techniques

defensive_countermeasures.corpus_awareness: On FEVER-like corpora, data extraction terms are highly anomalous
defensive_countermeasures.semantic_drift: Documents optimized for specific queries show unusual embedding patterns
defensive_countermeasures.temporal_monitoring: Recently added documents with high retrieval rates warrant investigation

scenario_3_prompt_injection.description: Conceptual example of poisoning to surface prompt manipulation techniques
scenario_3_prompt_injection.benign_distractors_concept: Legitimate topics: Prompt engineering, safety guardrails, RLHF alignment

sleeper_document_concept.purpose: Semantic bridge between legitimate prompt engineering and attacks

defensive_countermeasures.query_pattern_differential: Most effective method - shows 3.7-62× advantage over other techniques depending on corpus
defensive_countermeasures.hybrid_retrieval_effectiveness: Gradient-optimized attacks achieve 0% success across all α ∈ [0.3, 0.7] in our experiments
defensive_countermeasures.monitoring_recommendation: Continuous query pattern analysis with threshold α ≤ 0.2

benign_document_examples.notice: These are LEGITIMATE examples showing what benign documents look like. Safe for public release.

security_stack_exchange_typical.title: Best practices for implementing MFA in enterprise environments
security_stack_exchange_typical.content_structure: Question about multi-factor authentication, answers discussing TOTP, SMS, hardware tokens, implementation challenges, user experience considerations
security_stack_exchange_typical.embedding_characteristics: High semantic overlap with authentication, security, enterprise topics. Contains technical security terminology naturally.

fever_wikipedia_typical.title: History of cryptography
fever_wikipedia_typical.content_structure: Encyclopedia article covering ancient ciphers, WWII Enigma, modern encryption, key historical figures
fever_wikipedia_typical.embedding_characteristics: General knowledge about cryptography history. Low technical density.

technical_corpora.examples: Security Stack Exchange, GitHub code repos, API documentation
technical_corpora.characteristics: High frequency of attack-related terms, diverse semantic space
technical_corpora.recommended_detection: Query Pattern Differential (F1: 0.171 in our experiments)
technical_corpora.why_hard: Attack keywords are naturally common, semantic diversity reduces anomaly detection effectiveness

general_knowledge_corpora.characteristics: Low frequency of attack-related terms, more uniform semantic space
general_knowledge_corpora.why_easier: Attack keywords are statistically rare, clear domain boundaries

universal_best_practices.primary_defense: Deploy hybrid BM25+vector retrieval with α ≤ 0.5 (architectural defense)
universal_best_practices.secondary_monitoring: Query Pattern Differential with corpus-appropriate thresholds
universal_best_practices.corpus_classification: Analyze corpus properties to select detection strategy
universal_best_practices.continuous_monitoring: Track retrieval patterns for recently added documents
universal_best_practices.incident_response: Establish procedures for investigating flagged documents

what_is_NOT_included: Gradient optimization code for adversarial generation
Specific malicious queries that could be weaponized
responsible_research_statement: This repository prioritizes defensive security research. Attack concepts are described at a level sufficient for understanding defenses, but insufficient for weaponization. Researchers needing more detail for legitimate defensive research should contact the authors directly with institutional verification.
